title: Aaron
lead: Moses' older brother, his spokesman before Pharaoh, Israel's first high priest, and the maker of the golden calf. His descendants, the kohanim, served at the altar, and Hebrews contrasts his priesthood with Christ's (Exodus 4:14–16; 28–29; 32; Numbers 17; 20:22–29; Hebrews 5:1–5; 7:11).

sections.b: Aaron first appears as Moses' fluent older brother, sent to speak for him (Exodus 4:14–16), and he stands beside Moses before Pharaoh and holds up his arms at the battle with Amalek (Exodus 17:12). Ordained as the first high priest (Leviticus 8–9), he loses two sons who offer strange fire (Leviticus 10:1–3). With Miriam he challenges Moses and is rebuked (Numbers 12). When Korah's rebels contest his priesthood, his staff alone buds (Numbers 16–17), and he stands between the dead and the living with incense to stop a plague (Numbers 16:46–48). Because of the waters of Meribah he dies on Mount Hor without entering the land (Numbers 20:12, 22–29). Psalm 133:2 pictures oil on his beard; Hebrews 5:4 and 7:11 contrast his line with Christ's priesthood.
